newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Convicted murderer in Brazil massacre absolved.
newsitem.headline: Convicted murderer in Brazil massacre absolved.

text.p: A former police officer convicted of murder in a shooting spree in which eight street children died was declared innocent on Thursday at his retrial.

Nelson Oliveira dos Santos Cunha, 29, was sentenced to 261 years in jail in November on eight charges of murder and one of attempted murder in the incident of four years ago. Under Brazilian law anyone sentenced to more than 20 years in jail for a crime has the automatic right to a retrial.

After all-night proceedings the seven-member Rio de Janeiro state court jury found him innocent on all eight counts of murder, a court official said. His conviction for attempted murder stands, however, and he will remain in prison to serve an 18-year sentence for that crime.

Six children were killed when men opened fire indiscriminately on about 70 children playing or sleeping on the steps of the Candelaria Church in downtown Rio early on July 23, 1993. Two others were killed earlier and left nearby, and six children also were injured in the shooting spree.
Cristina Leonardo, an assistant prosecution lawyer and human rights activist, said the retrial was a disgrace, showing Brazil still quietly approved of police violence against society's outcasts.

"As a citizen and human rights lawyer I am indignant," she said. "The children have been victimised twice, once by the death squad and once by our prejudiced society which thinks street children should die."
Leonardo said the prosecution would appeal the outcome of the retrial.

Cunha, who left the Rio police force after the massacre, confessed his role in the killings in April 1996, just before the first of five men accused of the massacre, Marcus Vinicius Borges Emmanuel, went on trial. Cunha said he, Emmanuel and two other police officers, one of whom has since been murdered and one who is awaiting trial, committed the killings.

In his testimony, he blamed the officer who has since been murdered for most of the killings but admitted to having accidentally shot and wounded one of the victims, Wagner dos Santos, who is also a key witness in the Candelaria trials.

Cunha said he was forced to participate in the shooting spree and never killed or wanted to kill anyone even though he did shoot at the children. His testimony helped free three other men accused of the Candelaria massacre.
